title: House of Leaves

vibeProfile.oneLine: A house bigger inside than out, told in a book that becomes a maze.

summary: A young man finds a dead neighbour's manuscript about a documentary film concerning a house that is bigger on the inside than the outside, and as he pieces it together the reading of it begins to unravel him too. Danielewski's cult novel is a labyrinth in every sense: footnotes swallow footnotes, text spirals and fractures across the page, and multiple unreliable narrators nest inside one another. Part haunted-house horror, part love story, part puzzle box, it is unlike anything else, demanding and genuinely disorienting.
whyReadIt: A book that becomes the labyrinth it describes. A demanding, one-of-a-kind experience for readers who want to get lost.

funFacts.text: Its typography is part of the story: pages spiral, invert and empty out to mirror the house's spaces.
